description:
WebRush â 6-Hour Frontend Hackathon
WebRush is a fully online, individual frontend hackathon where participants get 6 hours to build a complete web solution for a given challenge.

But thereâs a twist â you don't get just one shot at your score.

The Challenge
At the beginning of the hackathon, one common problem statement will be provided to all participants.

Your task is to design and develop the best possible frontend solution within the 6-hour time limit.

You can choose your own approach, design, frontend framework, libraries, and tools â but your final submission must follow the challenge requirements.

Automated Evaluation with FAIE Engine
Your project will be evaluated automatically using the FAIE Engine, an automated frontend evaluation and scoring system.

The evaluation focuses on aspects such as:

UI/UX & Visual Quality
Required Features & Functionality
Code Quality & Structure
Responsiveness
Accessibility & Performance
Project Documentation
Overall implementation of the given challenge
No manual judging panel is required for scoring. Your submission is analyzed and scored through the evaluation engine.

3 Chances to Improve Your Score
Every participant gets up to 3 chances to submit and improve their project during the allowed submission window.

You can use these attempts strategically:

Build â Evaluate â Improve â Resubmit

Each evaluation provides a score, allowing you to identify areas that need improvement and work towards a better final score.

Your highest valid score will be considered for the final leaderboard.

Leaderboard = Final Results
This isn't just about completing the challenge â your score determines your position.

Participants will be ranked on the final leaderboard based on their highest achieved score.

Highest Rank â Winner
Second Highest Rank â Runner-Up
Other top-ranked participants â As per the final leaderboard

ï¸ Technology Rules
Individual participation only.
Fully online hackathon.
Frontend development only.
Modern frontend frameworks, libraries, UI tools, and development tools are allowed.
Backend technologies and backend implementation are not allowed.
The project must be developed within the 6-hour hackathon duration.
Previously built projects cannot be submitted.
Submission
Participants will submit:

Live deployed website
GitHub repository
Required project details
All submissions must be made within the specified hackathon timeline.

One Challenge. Six Hours. Three Chances. One Leaderboard.
Build fast. Get evaluated. Improve your score. Climb the leaderboard.

Welcome to WebRush.

problemDescription:
Problem Statement
Your Life, In Receipts
The Concept

Your digital life is made up of hundreds of tiny moments.

A song you played at 2 AM.
A place you visited.
A photo you took.
Something you bought.
A movie you watched.
A message you saved.
A search you made.
A random note you wrote.

Individually, these moments may not mean much.

But when you put them together, they tell a story.

The Challenge

Build a frontend-only digital experience that transforms a collection of fictional âlife receiptsâ into a meaningful and interactive story.

Every participant will receive the same dataset containing different types of digital-life activities:

Music
Movies & Entertainment
Places
Purchases
Photos
Messages
Searches
Events
Personal Notes

The dataset represents fragments of someone's digital life over a period of time.

Your task is not simply to display these records.

You must explore the data, identify meaningful connections, discover patterns, and turn those disconnected moments into a story that the user can understand and interact with.

The Core Challenge

Think about what could be hidden inside the data.

What kind of person was the user during different periods?

How did their interests and behaviour change over time?

Which moments are connected?

What recurring patterns can be found?

Can unrelated-looking receipts reveal a bigger story when viewed together?

Your experience should move beyond:

Raw Data â Information

and aim for:

Raw Data â Insights â Connections â Story

How you achieve this is entirely up to you.

Don't Just Build a Timeline

A simple chronological list of receipts is not enough.

We don't want:

January â February â March â April

with a collection of cards underneath.

Think about the relationships between different types of information.

For example:

Song â Location â Photo â Purchase â Event

might appear to be five unrelated records.

But together, they could represent one meaningful moment or chapter in someone's life.

Your interface should make these connections discoverable, interactive, and meaningful.

Minimum Requirements

Your solution must provide:

A way to explore the provided life receipts
Meaningful filtering, searching, or navigation
At least one meaningful mechanism for discovering relationships or patterns
An interactive storytelling experience
A clear visual representation of the user's digital journey
Responsive design across different screen sizes

These requirements define the minimum experience.

How you solve the problem is completely up to you.

Creative Direction

Your solution could take the form of:

Digital Scrapbook
Interactive Timeline
Life Map
Data Story
Personal Museum
Interactive Journal
Game-like Experience
Data Visualization
AI-inspired Interface
Or something completely new

These are only examples â you are not required to follow any of them.

We want to see your interpretation of the problem.

The Real Challenge

You have a dataset full of disconnected moments.

Your job is to give those moments meaning.

Don't just show the user:

âWhat happened?â

Help them discover:

âWhat does it all mean?â

The strongest solutions will make the user curious enough to explore, connect the dots, and discover something they didn't notice at first glance.

The Constraint

You have exactly 6 hours to:

Understand â Design â Build â Refine â Deploy

Your solution must be created within the hackathon duration.

This is a frontend-only challenge. You are free to use modern frontend frameworks, libraries, UI tools, and development tools of your choice.

Backend implementation is not required and is not permitted.

Your Mission

One Dataset.
Hundreds of Moments.
Infinite Stories.
Six Hours to Uncover One.

What story will you uncover?
rules: Participation is strictly individual. Team participation is not allowed.
WebRush is a fully online, 6-hour frontend-only hackathon.
Participants must build their solution within the given 6-hour hackathon window.
Only frontend technologies, frameworks, libraries, and development tools are allowed.
Backend technologies, backend servers, databases, and server-side implementations are not allowed.
All participants will receive the same problem statement and must build their solution according to the given challenge.
Participants must use the dataset provided by the organizers for the challenge.
Previously developed or pre-built projects cannot be submitted. The project must be created during the hackathon.
Participants may use sample/mock data where required, but the final solution must remain frontend-only.
The submitted project must be responsive and accessible through a working live deployment.
A maximum of 3 submission attempts will be allowed for improving the project, subject to the submission window specified by the organizers.
The FAIE Engine will evaluate submissions based on the predefined evaluation framework and technical criteria.
Only valid submissions that meet the hackathon requirements will be considered for the final leaderboard.
All participants must follow the official communication channels for important announcements and hackathon updates.
The final leaderboard and results will be based on the valid evaluation scores recorded by the FAIE Engine.
Submissions will be automatically evaluated using the FAIE (Frontend Arena Intelligence Engine).
Participants must submit both a live deployment URL and GitHub repository before the submission deadline
